doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Jazz, its audience and the 1953 records
title: The 1953 Gramercy Five with Hank Jones, Tommy Potter and Tal Farlow
summary: The group made good music but no label wanted it, and his Modern Music for Clarinet sold almost nothing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: This is the Gramercy Five with . . .

Yeah, with Hank Jones, Tommy Potter, and Tal Farlow. That group. We were making damn good music, but in 1953 no-one wanted it. The recording companies, from Columbia through RCA through every company. Nope. They couldn’t see a market for it. There was no market for it. The recording I made, called Modern Music for Clarinet, I put in a year and a half, getting that stuff together. It probably sold 12 copies or 12 and a half. I don’t know.
